increments.title: Coverage inventory script with covered-cells diff and worklist
increments.goal: A static coverage inventory (`scripts/evaluator-coverage-inventory.js`) that parses the whole fixture corpus, extracts every occurring rule-construct combination cell, diffs it against a machine-readable record of covered cells, and writes the uncovered cells to `docs/testing/worklist.json` — so the two skills of the later increments have a mechanical source of truth to work from.
criteria: `scripts/evaluator-coverage-inventory.js` exists and parses every `.cat`/`.gst` file of both fixture sets (`src/evaluator/__fixtures__/whfb6-definitive/` and `src/__fixtures__/whfb6/`) statically, without rosters and without running the evaluator.

It records every occurring combination cell with occurrence count and file locations along these axes: constraint field-class x scope x flags (`shared`, `includeChildSelections`, `includeChildForces`, `percentValue`); condition type x scope x field-class; repeat attributes; modifier type x target-field-class; and the nesting constructs (`conditionGroup` types including `not`, `modifierGroups`, nested `repeats`).
The record of covered cells is machine-readable and the script diffs the inventory against it automatically; no human or agent has to read `docs/testing/constraint-matrix.md` inside the loop.
The uncovered cells are written to `docs/testing/worklist.json`.
The script exits non-zero when the worklist is non-empty and zero when every occurring cell is covered.
The cell extraction is covered by unit tests, and they pass.

return.plan:
# Increment 1 — static coverage inventory, covered-cells diff, worklist

## What gets built

Three new source artefacts and one seeded data file:

1. `scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-cells.js` — the whole logic, pure and side-effect free at module level: classifiers, cell extraction from parsed XML documents, corpus walking, coverage derivation, diff, worklist building, exit-code rule.
2. `scripts/evaluator-coverage-inventory.js` — a thin CLI: installs jsdom's `DOMParser`, calls the lib, writes `docs/testing/worklist.json`, prints a summary, sets the exit code. Mirrors the existing pair `scripts/lib/evaluator-measurement.js` + `scripts/measure-evaluator.js`.
3. `docs/testing/covered-cells.json` — the machine-readable manual record of covered cells (seeded, see below).
4. `docs/testing/worklist.json` — generated output, committed.

Plus two test files (see `testPlan`) and a two-line pointer at the top of `docs/testing/constraint-matrix.md` saying the machine-readable record is now `covered-cells.json` + `worklist.json` and the matrix is human context only, never read inside the loop.

Write everything in English (comments, JSDoc, test names), even though neighbouring files are German — the shared brief overrides the local convention.

## Hard constraints that shape the design

- **No evaluator import.** `.dependency-cruiser.cjs` rule `evaluator-nur-ueber-fassade` has severity `error`: anything outside `src/evaluator/` may import only `src/evaluator/evaluator.js`. So the script must NOT import `src/evaluator/model.js` for `CountedFieldKind`/`ScopeKeyword`, however tempting. It defines its own vocabulary. This is also the right call in substance: the inventory is data-first and must stay independent of the engine (ADR 0033's black-box principle).
- **No roster, no evaluation.** Only `.cat`/`.gst` text is read; no `.ros`, no `evaluate()` call.
- **`scripts/**/*` is type-checked.** `tsconfig.json` includes `scripts/**/*` with `checkJs: true` (tests excluded via `**/*.test.js`). Both new source files need JSDoc types that satisfy `tsc --noEmit`.
- **`docs/testing/` is scanned by the E2E runner.** `src/evaluator/e2e.testcatalog.test.js:212` filters `readdirSync(..., {withFileTypes:true})` to `entry.isDirectory()`, so new *files* directly under `docs/testing/` are ignored by it. Safe.

## XML parsing

Use jsdom's `DOMParser`, exactly as `scripts/measure-evaluator.js` does (`globalThis.DOMParser = new JSDOM().window.DOMParser`). Measured on the real corpus: all nine files parse in **1.8 s total** (largest file 2.4 MB). A hand-rolled tag scanner was considered and rejected — it buys a second or two and risks false positives on tag-like text; jsdom is already a devDependency and already the project's Node-side XML seam.

The lib never touches `DOMParser` itself: its entry point takes already-parsed documents (`[{ file, doc }]`) or a `parseXml` callback. That is what makes the extraction unit-testable on small XML strings, and it lets the vitest jsdom environment supply the parser in tests without importing jsdom there.

After parsing, check each document for a `parsererror` element and fail loudly (exit 2) instead of silently reporting zero cells.

## Corpus

Two directories, `.cat`/`.gst` only (each also holds a `README.md`, which is skipped):
- `src/evaluator/__fixtures__/whfb6-definitive/` — 4 `.cat` + 1 `.gst`
- `src/__fixtures__/whfb6/` — 3 `.cat` + 1 `.gst`

Nine files. Paths in the output are repo-relative and POSIX-separated, so the JSON is stable across machines. Derive the repo root from the module location (`fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)`), like the other scripts do, so the run does not depend on the working directory.

## Symbol tables (first pass)

One pass over all documents collects, across the whole corpus (not per file — cost types live in the `.gst`, constraints in the `.cat`s):
- `costTypeIds` from every `<costType id=…>` (3 in this corpus),
- `characteristicTypeIds` from every `<characteristicType id=…>` (27),
- `constraintIds` from every `<constraint id=…>` (4365), together with the element, so a scenario's `limitId` can be looked up,
- an id→element index is only needed for constraints.

These tables are what turns a raw GUID in a `field` attribute into a class.

## Axis vocabularies

**Scope class** (`constraint`/`condition`/`repeat`): the literal keyword if it is one of `roster`, `force`, `parent`, `self`, `unit`, `ancestor`, `primary-catalogue`, `category`; a GUID (anything else non-empty) collapses to `id`; a missing attribute is `absent`. Source: `docs/battlescribe-data-format.md` §13.1 and the `scope="unit"`/`scope="ancestor"` box in §7.7. Collapsing GUIDs is essential — the corpus holds 8 distinct id-scopes and keeping them apart would make the worklist a list of catalogue rows instead of a list of constructs. In this corpus `category` never occurs as a literal.

**Counted field class** (`constraint`/`condition`/`repeat` `field`, per §13.2): `selections`→`selectionCount`, `forces`→`forceCount`, `limit::<id>`→`limitValue`, an id in `costTypeIds`→`costSum`, anything else→`unresolvedField`, missing→`absent`.

**Modifier target field class** (`modifier` `field`, per §7.7/§13.2): the literals `hidden`, `name`, `category`, `error`, `warning`, `info`, `sortIndex`, `page` stay themselves; an id in `costTypeIds`→`costValue`; in `characteristicTypeIds`→`characteristic`; in `constraintIds`→`constraintValue`; `limit::<id>`→`limitValue`; anything else→`unresolvedTarget`; missing→`absent`. **Finding:** three modifier `field` ids in the corpus (`ce6e-afde-2ed1-aac2`, `a59d-2ddb-429c-1aca`, `410e-ed97-ecf8-cfa4`, 7 occurrences) exist nowhere in the corpus as an `id` attribute — dangling references. They must land in one `unresolvedTarget` bucket, not one cell each, and the raw ids belong in that cell's examples.

**childId class** (`condition`/`repeat`, per §13.2): `model`, `unit`, `upgrade`, `any` stay literal; anything else non-empty→`id`; missing→`absent`.

**Flag normalization — the single most important decision.** An omitted `shared`/`includeChildSelections`/`includeChildForces`/`percentValue`/`roundUp` is normalized to the XSD default before it enters the key: `shared=true`, `includeChildSelections=false`, `includeChildForces=false`, `percentValue=false` (`src/parser/schema/Catalogue.xsd:428-431`), `roundUp=false` (`Catalogue.xsd:545`). Without it the corpus splits into cells that differ only in serialization noise — measured: 32 raw constraint cells collapse to **22** normalized ones, and the two largest "different" cells (2523 and 542 occurrences) are the same cell. Put the defaults in one frozen constant with the XSD line numbers in the comment. `repeats` is `use="required"` in the XSD and is bucketed `1` vs `gt1` instead of being normalized.

## The cell key

A `|`-joined string, stable and greppable, with the same axes also present structurally on the record. Seven kinds:

- `constraint|<type>|<fieldClass>|<scopeClass>|s=<shared>|ics=<includeChildSelections>|icf=<includeChildForces>|pct=<percentValue>`
- `condition|<type>|<scopeClass>|<fieldClass>|child=<childIdClass>`
- `repeat|<fieldClass>|<scopeClass>|child=<childIdClass>|repeats=<1|gt1>|roundUp=<flag>|pct=<flag>`
- `modifier|<type>|<targetFieldClass>`
- `conditionGroup|<type>|<top|nested>` — `nested` when the group's grandparent element is itself a `conditionGroup` (`conditionGroup > conditionGroups > conditionGroup`)
- `modifierGroup|cond=<bool>|repeats=<bool>|<top|nested>` — `cond` is true when the group carries a `<conditions>` or `<conditionGroups>` child, `repeats` when it carries a `<repeats>` child, `nested` by the same grandparent rule
- `repeatList|n=<1|gt1>|on=<modifier|modifierGroup>` — one per `<repeats>` list element; this is the axis that distinguishes "several `<repeat>` in one list" from a single one

Two deliberate departures from the criteria's literal wording, both recorded here as decisions:
- **Constraint `type` (`min`/`max`) is part of the constraint key** although the criterion names only field-class × scope × flags. `min` and `max` are different code paths and the matrix's first two rows are exactly this; leaving it out would merge them. Costs nothing (22 cells).
- **`childId` class is part of the condition key** although the criterion names only type × scope × field-class. §7.7 documents two encodings of a `forceEntry` instance check (`scope=<forceId> childId=any` vs `scope=force childId=<forceId>`), and type-keyword counting (`model`/`unit`/`upgrade`) is a distinct path from id counting (Issue 078). Costs about 11 extra cells (39 instead of ~28). Every criterion still holds — the cells are recorded along the named axes, only refined.

Rejected alternatives: keeping raw scope/field GUIDs as their own cells (turns 101 cells into hundreds of catalogue rows); one cell per dangling modifier target id (same problem); a `conditionGroup` axis for member fan-out (the matrix already records that fan-out is not a separate code path).

**Measured result of this design on today's corpus: 101 distinct cells** — constraint 22, condition 39, repeat 7, modifier 22, conditionGroup 5, modifierGroup 4, repeatList 2, over 9375 construct occurrences. That is a worklist a campaign can actually work down; it is the number the implementation should reproduce.

## Cell record

Per cell: `key`, `kind`, `axes` (the structured components), `occurrences` (total), `files` (`[{ file, occurrences }]`, sorted by path) and `examples` — at most **3**, in corpus/document order, each `{ file, elementId, anchorTag, anchorId, anchorName, path }` where the anchor is the nearest ancestor element carrying both `id` and `name` (the `selectionEntry`/`categoryEntry`/`forceEntry`/`entryLink` the construct hangs on) and `path` is the tag chain from the document root joined by `>`.

jsdom gives no line numbers, so "file locations" are file path + anchor id/name instead. That is deliberately more useful to the black-box scenario author of increment 2, who searches the catalogue by id, than a line number would be.

## Where "covered" comes from

Two sources, unioned:

1. **Derived automatically from the existing scenario manifests, on every run.** Every `docs/testing/*/scenario.json` declares `rosters[].expect.firing[].limitId` and `rosters[].expect.absent[]` (a plain id string). Those ids are constraint ids. Look each one up in the constraint index and mark that constraint's cell covered, with the scenario directory name as evidence. Measured: 38 manifests pin 73 distinct ids, 70 of which resolve to a constraint, and they cover **15 of the 22** constraint cells. This is what puts the existing coverage into the loop mechanically, without anyone reading `constraint-matrix.md` — and it can never go stale, because it is recomputed rather than transcribed. An id that resolves to nothing is reported as an unmatched-evidence line, never a crash.
2. **`docs/testing/covered-cells.json`, the manual record** — for cells no manifest id can attest (condition, modifier, repeat, group families) and for waived cells. Shape: `{ "schemaVersion": 1, "cells": [ { "key": "…", "evidence": ["docs/testing/<scenario>" | "unit test <path> <name>"], "rationale": "…" } ] }`. This is the file increment 2's skill appends to when it lands a green scenario.

**Seed the manual record with exactly one entry** and nothing more: `condition|greaterThanOrEqualTo|parent|selectionCount|child=id`, one occurrence (Orcs and Goblins, "ergofang"), rationale: not an XSD condition type (`docs/battlescribe-data-format.md` §13.1), reported as `unsupportedCondition` and evaluated fail-closed — there is no catalogue-derivable semantics to pin. Do **not** transcribe the rest of `constraint-matrix.md` into the record: its rows are per-attribute prose, not per-cell, and a guessed seed would silently hide genuinely uncovered cells. Fail-closed is the project's own principle here — an over-large worklist costs the campaign work, a wrong seed costs it a blind spot.

Expected first worklist: about **85** cells (101 minus 15 derived minus 1 waived).

## Diff, output, exit code

`docs/testing/worklist.json`:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "generatedBy": "scripts/evaluator-coverage-inventory.js",
  "corpus": ["src/evaluator/__fixtures__/whfb6-definitive", "src/__fixtures__/whfb6"],
  "totals": { "cells": 101, "covered": 16, "uncovered": 85 },
  "cells": [ …the uncovered cell records… ]
}
```

Sorted by `occurrences` descending, then `key` ascending — deterministic. **No timestamp and no run id**: a generated file that changes on every run would dirty the working tree forever and make the drift guard impossible.

Stdout: one summary block — cells by kind, covered by derivation, covered by record, uncovered, plus any stale or unmatched evidence — then the top uncovered cells. Warnings never change the exit code.

Exit codes: **0** when the worklist is empty, **1** when it is not, **2** on an operational failure (a corpus directory missing, a `parsererror`, unreadable JSON). Two guards report but do not fail: a key in `covered-cells.json` that no longer occurs in the corpus (stale), and a key whose syntax does not parse. Deadlocking the loop on bookkeeping is worse than a warning line.

**Running the script today exits 1, and that is the correct outcome** — the worklist is non-empty by construction until the campaign of increments 2 and 3 has run. It is therefore deliberately not one of the `checks`; the drift-guard test covers the same ground without a red gate.

## Order of work

1. lib: classifiers + `cellKey` + extraction over injected documents.
2. lib: corpus walk, manifest-derived coverage, manual record read, diff, worklist build, exit-code rule.
3. CLI wrapper.
4. Seed `docs/testing/covered-cells.json`; run the CLI once to generate `docs/testing/worklist.json`; commit both.
5. Pointer line in `docs/testing/constraint-matrix.md`.

Note that `package.json` declares `engines.node: ^24` while the container runs Node v22.22.2 — `npm ci`, `node` scripts and jsdom all worked anyway; no action needed, just do not be surprised.

Commands used by the test plan and the checks, all from the repository root:

- `npx vitest run scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-cells.test.js` — the unit tests of the cell extraction, alone.
- `npx vitest run scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-corpus.test.js` — the real-corpus drift guard, alone.

- `npx oxlint scripts/` — the repo's linter, scoped to the changed directory (`npm run lint` would run it over the whole repository).
- `npm run depcruise` — `depcruise src scripts e2e`; the ADR-0030 clean-room rules have severity `error` and are what would catch an accidental `src/evaluator/*` import from the new script. Other rule violations are warn-only and do not affect the exit code.

There is no formatter in this repository (no prettier configuration). `npm run knip` exists but is warn-only and not part of this increment.
return.testPlan:
## Whether

Tests are needed. The extraction is pure logic over XML and the criteria demand unit tests for it.

## Conventions and their documentation

**There is no test-suite doc and no `CLAUDE.md` in any test directory.** The only `CLAUDE.md` in the repository is the root one (a symlink to `.agents/AGENTS.md`); `docs/testing/` holds scenario directories and `constraint-matrix.md`, no agent doc. The nearest thing to a suite doc is ADR 0006 (`docs/adr/0006-testing-and-automation.md`), which fixes vitest as the unit framework, the zero-tolerance rule, and the `docs/testing/` manifest runner — but says nothing about how a `scripts/` test is written. Write the missing directory doc as part of the test step if the role calls for it; nothing existing contradicts what follows.

Observed conventions to follow, from `scripts/lib/evaluator-measurement.test.js`, `scripts/generate-schema-module.test.js` and `scripts/rules-crawler.test.js`: named imports from `vitest` (`describe, it, expect`), the module under test imported relatively, no global setup beyond `vitest.config.js` (environment `jsdom`, globals on, `src/test-utils/i18nTestSetup.js`). Because the environment is jsdom, **`DOMParser` is already a global in tests** — the test files need no jsdom import of their own; build documents with `new DOMParser().parseFromString(xml, 'application/xml')`. Existing script tests carry German comments; write yours in English, per the shared brief.

Nothing is faked or mocked: the lib is pure and the corpus is a frozen fixture.

## What — file 1: `scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-cells.test.js`

Unit tests over tiny synthetic XML strings (a `<catalogue>` root with a handful of constructs, plus `<costType>`/`<characteristicType>` declarations where a class depends on them). Level: unit. Framework: vitest. Command: `npx vitest run scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-cells.test.js`.

Criterion "records every occurring combination cell … along these axes":

1. A constraint `type=max field=selections scope=parent shared=true includeChildSelections=false includeChildForces=false percentValue=false` yields exactly the key `constraint|max|selectionCount|parent|s=true|ics=false|icf=false|pct=false`, with `occurrences` 1 and the given file path recorded.
2. Flag normalization: the same constraint with `includeChildForces` and `percentValue` omitted yields the **same** key, and the two occurrences merge into one cell with `occurrences` 2 and both files listed.
3. Explicit non-default flags are not collapsed: `shared="false"` yields a key distinct from `shared="true"`.
4. `type="min"` and `type="max"` on otherwise identical constraints yield two cells.
5. Counted field classes: `selections`→`selectionCount`; `forces`→`forceCount`; an id declared as `<costType>`→`costSum`; `limit::<that id>`→`limitValue`; an id declared nowhere→`unresolvedField`; the attribute missing→`absent`.
6. Scope classes: each of `roster`, `force`, `parent`, `self`, `unit`, `ancestor`, `primary-catalogue`, `category` stays literal; a GUID-shaped value→`id`; missing→`absent`.
7. Condition cell: `condition|<type>|<scopeClass>|<fieldClass>|child=<childIdClass>`, checked for at least `instanceOf` and `atLeast`; `childId` `model`/`any` stay literal, a GUID→`id`, missing→`absent`.
8. Repeat cell: field, scope and childId classes as above, plus `repeats="1"`→`repeats=1` and `repeats="3"`→`repeats=gt1`, `roundUp` omitted→`roundUp=false`, `percentValue` carried through.
9. Modifier cell: `hidden`, `name`, `category`, `error` stay literal; a `<costType>` id→`costValue`; a `<characteristicType>` id→`characteristic`; a `<constraint>` id declared elsewhere in the same corpus→`constraintValue`; an id declared nowhere→`unresolvedTarget`, with the raw id preserved in the cell's examples.
10. `conditionGroup` cells for `and`, `or` and `not`; a group directly under a modifier's `<conditionGroups>` is `top`, a group inside another group's `<conditionGroups>` is `nested`.
11. `modifierGroup` cells: `cond=true` when the group carries `<conditions>`, `cond=true` when it carries `<conditionGroups>` instead, `cond=false` when it carries neither; `repeats=true` when it carries `<repeats>`; `nested` when it sits inside another `modifierGroup`.
12. `repeatList` cells: a `<repeats>` with one `<repeat>`→`n=1`, with two→`n=gt1`; `on=modifier` versus `on=modifierGroup`.
13. Occurrence counting and locations: the same cell occurring three times across two files reports `occurrences` 3 and per-file counts; `examples` is capped at 3 and each example carries the element's own id (or null), the nearest named ancestor's tag/id/name, and the root-to-element tag path.

Edges:

14. A document with no rule constructs yields an empty inventory (not a throw).
15. A constraint with every optional attribute omitted still yields a fully defaulted key.
16. A document containing a `parsererror` element is reported as an operational failure, not counted.

Criterion "the record of covered cells is machine-readable and the script diffs the inventory against it automatically":

17. `coveredKeysFromManifests`: a manifest whose `rosters[].expect.firing[].limitId` names a constraint present in the corpus yields that constraint's cell key with the scenario directory as evidence; an id in `rosters[].expect.absent[]` does the same; an id that names no constraint is returned as unmatched evidence and does not throw.
18. `diffCells`: a covered key removes its cell from the uncovered list; a covered key that occurs nowhere in the inventory comes back as `stale` without failing; an empty covered record leaves every cell uncovered.
19. The manual record is parsed from the documented shape (`schemaVersion`, `cells[].key/evidence/rationale`) and its keys join the derived ones.

Criterion "exits non-zero when the worklist is non-empty and zero when every occurring cell is covered":

20. `exitCodeFor` returns 1 for a worklist with at least one cell and 0 for an empty one. Test it as a pure function; do not spawn the CLI.

## What — file 2: `scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-corpus.test.js`

Integration level, against the real frozen corpus (about 2 s of parsing). Framework: vitest. Command: `npx vitest run scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-corpus.test.js`. Parse the corpus once in a `beforeAll`.

Criterion "parses every `.cat`/`.gst` file of both fixture sets statically, without rosters and without running the evaluator":

21. The corpus walk returns exactly nine files — five under `src/evaluator/__fixtures__/whfb6-definitive/` and four under `src/__fixtures__/whfb6/` — with the `README.md` of each directory excluded, and no document reports a `parsererror`.
22. Per-kind occurrence totals match a plain tag count of the corpus: constraint 5290, condition 1739, conditionGroup 261, modifier 1762, modifierGroup 109, repeat 214. These come from `grep -o '<constraint ' -r <both fixture dirs> | wc -l` and friends, run during research on the frozen fixtures. If a number disagrees, re-run that grep before touching the extraction — the fixtures are frozen, so a mismatch is a real extraction bug, but the grep is the arbiter.
23. Landmark cells the corpus is known to contain are present: `conditionGroup|not|nested` (2 occurrences, Vampire Counts), a `condition|greaterThanOrEqualTo|…` cell (1 occurrence), a `modifier|…|unresolvedTarget` cell, and at least one cell of each of the seven kinds.

Criterion "the uncovered cells are written to `docs/testing/worklist.json`":

24. Drift guard, modelled on `scripts/generate-schema-module.test.js`: recompute the worklist from the corpus, the manifests and `docs/testing/covered-cells.json`, and assert it deep-equals the committed `docs/testing/worklist.json`. This is what proves the committed file is the script's own output and stays honest as scenarios land.
25. The committed worklist's `totals` are internally consistent: `covered + uncovered === cells`, and `cells` array length equals `totals.uncovered`.
26. The worklist ordering is deterministic: recomputing twice yields identical JSON, and cells are ordered by `occurrences` descending then `key` ascending.

## Deliberately untested, and why

It alternates phase A (the inverted explorer working through the worklist) with phase B (run `uroboros:agile-loop` on a campaign issue whose task list is the current set of red scenarios), and re-runs phase A after every phase B round.
It terminates when the worklist is empty, every evaluator E2E scenario is green, and no parked question is open.
At the end of every unfinished run it re-arms the loop with `send_later` about one hour ahead, and stops re-arming once the termination criterion holds.
Each run is capped at a fixed number of cells, and a cell is parked after two failed implementation rounds instead of being retried again.
All campaign state lives in files (worklist, parked questions, campaign issue) so a fresh session resumes from disk alone.
Parked questions are reported to the human at the end of a run, and their recorded answers are folded back in before the parked cells are retried.
